summary: The register lists the McVay site in Clarke County under the Alabama Forestry Commission; only the stands and one antenna-era building are described.

facts.status_note: Only the stands and one vandalized building remain, according to the register.

evidence.supports: stands remain; building from antenna use, badly vandalized
evidence.quote: Stands are all that remain. One badly vandilized building from when tower was used as antenna site also at this spot.

evidence.supports: later fitted with antennae that remain on many firetowers
evidence.quote: eventually fitted with antennae for communications, which remain on many firetowers to this day.

sources.title: McVay Fire Tower Site
sources.publisher: Former Fire Lookout Sites register (Forest Fire Lookout Association)

sources.title: Thomas Kaufmann: Keeping Alabama's historic lookout towers

notes_for_editor: Thin record: the register entry and a stub page. Two searches found no build, height, staffing or fate history beyond the register. A tower-database listing (allbluebook.com) names a McVay Lookout Tower in Jackson, Clarke County, but the page returned only its title, so it is not cited. The 1819 News feature is state context, not site evidence. Nothing read says whether the land is open to visitors.
